transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net mobile customer support, my name is Chloe. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Chloe. I'm really confused and quite concerned. My monthly forty-gigabyte mobile data allowance has completely run out just five days into my new billing cycle, and I don't understand how that could possibly happen.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly help you inspect your mobile data usage logs, Elijah. Before we inspect the network data logs, could you confirm your full name and billing address for account verification?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Elijah Wood, 14 King Street, Manchester, M2 4WQ.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Elijah. I can certainly understand your concern when an entire month's data allowance disappears so quickly, so let's look into your account usage together and find out what caused that spike. And can you verify the four-digit security PIN on the mobile account, Elijah?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is 5519.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, verification is complete. So what I understand is your monthly allowance of forty gigabytes was fully consumed within five days of your billing refresh, and you need to understand where that usage went and get your data connectivity restored, is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. I woke up this morning to a text message saying I had zero megabytes remaining, and all my apps stopped loading.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What handset model are you currently using, Elijah?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's an iPhone 15 Pro.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did you recently change any camera settings or record high-definition video over the weekend?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Now that you mention it, I was at my sister's wedding on Saturday and filmed about an hour of 4K video clips.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And do you have iCloud Photos or Google Photos backup enabled on your phone?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I use iCloud Photos, yes. Everything usually backs up automatically.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me for a moment while I pull up the network data session timestamps on our billing gateway.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Elijah. Looking at the session breakdown, on Sunday night between eleven PM and three AM, there was a continuous forty-two gigabyte upload session over cellular 5G.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh no! My home Wi-Fi must have disconnected while I was sleeping, so the iPhone backed up the entire 4K wedding footage over the 5G cellular network!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That explains it completely. An hour of 4K sixty-frames-per-second video is roughly forty to forty-five gigabytes of raw data.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there a way to prevent the phone from ever doing that again over mobile data?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, absolutely. Grab your iPhone now and I will walk you through turning off cellular sync.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've got the phone unlocked and in my hand.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open 'Settings', tap 'Photos', and scroll down to 'Cellular Data'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Found it. 'Cellular Data' toggle is currently switched on in green.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Tap that toggle to turn it off. That will ensure photo and video library syncs only happen when connected to Wi-Fi.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Switched off now. That's a huge relief. I don't want another surprise like that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let's check your low data mode under cellular settings to give you extra protection.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Where is that located?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Also, does your home Wi-Fi network have a strong signal in your bedroom where the phone charges overnight?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's a bit patchy up on the second floor, to be honest. The router is down in the hallway.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That explains why the phone dropped back to 5G during the overnight backup. If the Wi-Fi signal drops below two bars, iOS automatically falls back to cellular if Wi-Fi Assist is enabled.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Aha! Wi-Fi Assist was probably on!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can check that under Cellular settings at the very bottom: toggle 'Wi-Fi Assist' off as well.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Just scrolled down and toggled Wi-Fi Assist off. That completely closes that loophole.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And your international roaming status remains active for when you travel abroad.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know roaming is enabled.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Go back to main 'Settings', tap 'Cellular', tap 'Cellular Data Options', and tap 'Data Mode'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I see 'Allow More Data on 5G', 'Standard', and 'Low Data Mode'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Selecting 'Standard' or 'Low Data Mode' stops background cloud synchronization whenever you're on cellular.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ticked 'Low Data Mode'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm the handset before I apply a data credit bolt-on, you are using the iPhone 15 Pro registered to SIM ending 881, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's the one.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously I cannot reset the consumed cellular traffic that was already uploaded to Apple's servers, but as a loyal customer on our Unlimited Plus tier, I can add a complimentary fifteen-gigabyte courtesy data bolt-on to carry you through the remaining twenty-five days of your cycle.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Really? That would be incredible Chloe! Does that cost anything extra?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, it's a completely free customer care adjustment applied to your current billing period.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You have no idea how much I appreciate that. I need mobile data for maps and train tickets while commuting.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The fifteen-gigabyte bolt-on has been provisioned on the HLR. Can you toggle Airplane Mode on for five seconds and toggle it off to refresh your network token?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Turning on Airplane Mode... Waiting five seconds... Turning it off... S-Net 5G icon is back at the top of the screen!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you try opening a webpage or checking your email app now to test data connectivity?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening BBC News... It loaded instantly! And my WhatsApp messages just synced up!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And if you open the My S-Net mobile app, you should see the fifteen-gigabyte bolt-on balance showing under remaining data.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening My S-Net app... Yes! 'Remaining data: 15.0 GB courtesy bolt-on'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to verify your notification preferences, your account is set to receive SMS alerts when you reach eighty percent and one hundred percent of your data allowance, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's how I got the warning text this morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Is there anything else with your mobile plan or allowances that I can help you with today, Elijah?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No Chloe, you explained everything so clearly and sorted out my data within minutes. Thank you so much!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was an absolute pleasure. Thank you for choosing S-Net, Elijah, and have a wonderful day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Chloe, goodbye.
